summary.text: Christopher Gallant is the Democratic nominee in New York's 1st District, challenging incumbent Republican Nick LaLota. He enlisted in the Army at 17, worked as an air traffic controller and now flies Black Hawk helicopters in the New York Army National Guard; he is also a volunteer firefighter and a former local air traffic controllers' union president. His Ballotpedia survey says he is running to make Long Island more affordable, improve medical access for seniors and veterans, strengthen infrastructure and restore accountability in Washington.

paragraphs.text: Gallant was born in Smithtown, New York, and lives in Amity Harbor, which is outside the 1st District; he has said he would not move into the district if elected.

He enlisted in the Army at age 17 and trained as an air traffic controller, deploying to Kuwait in 2012. He earned a bachelor's degree from Dowling College in 2014; the VoteVets profile describes his degree as one in Aviation Management.
Gallant worked as an FAA air traffic controller, most recently at Kennedy Airport, and served as local president of the National Air Traffic Controllers Association.

He later became a Black Hawk pilot in the New York Army National Guard. According to the VoteVets profile, his service has included directing emergency operations at the Javits Center during the COVID-19 pandemic and providing air support to the Secret Service during presidential campaigns, and he deployed again in 2022. He also served as an Equal Opportunity representative in the U.S. Army.

Gallant is a volunteer firefighter with the Copiague Fire Department. He is affiliated with the Veterans of Foreign Wars, where Politics NY describes him as a post leader, as well as the American Legion and the Army Aviation Association of America, among other organizations.
He won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary over Lukas Ventouras, 62.9% to 37.0%.
